full_judgment: IV. The learned Advocate lastly submits that it is in the evidence on record that though the plaintiffs prayed for recovery of possession in respect of 0.05½ acre of land of suit plot No. 913, they did not pray for recovery of possession in respect of the dispossessed land of suit plot No. 914, but when the plaintiffs have paid ad valorem Court-fee for the entire suit land, then as title of the plaintiffs has been found in the entire suit land, there is no bar to decree the suit and to that effect reliance was made before the High Court Division upon placing the case reported in 3 BLC 502 wherein it has been held that "in a suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession where the plaintiff has paid ad valorem court fees for the entire suit land, if her title is established in the entire suit land she is entitled to get recovery of possession of the entire suit land and since she is already in possession of major portion of the suit land she is entitled to get recovery of possession of that portion of land which is in possession of the defendant", but the High Court Division has failed to discuss the said principle of law and also failed to appreciate the said principle of law, though the lower appellate Court appreciated the principle of law and came to a correct decision."
